- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict sharp upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often overpredicts downward moves; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day for 3–7 days post-spike.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence; if below, increase by 1–2% per day.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model often misjudges momentum; use sentiment swing as trigger for 3-day lag correction: forecast = previous day’s + sentiment-weighted deviation (0.3×sentiment + 0.7×history).
- For 30-day forecasts, model underestimates volatility in low-sentiment periods; add 0.5–1.5% volatility buffer if sentiment <0.33 over last 7 days.
- If true outcome deviates >5% from 30-day forecast, check if sentiment was >0.67 3–5 days prior — if yes, model likely missed bullish momentum; adjust forecast up by 1–2% for next 7 days.
